nodes.label: Development Phases (0-20)
nodes.rationale: Do not skip phases merely to make a demo look complete.

nodes.label: Required Documentation Set
nodes.rationale: Documentation must not become disconnected from implementation.

nodes.label: Environment Verification
nodes.rationale: OS, CPU, compiler, SDK, package manager, build system, Python, Git, audio/MIDI libraries and plugin SDKs must be determined without installing anything.

nodes.label: Feature Roadmap (Phase 0-20)
nodes.rationale: The roadmap is proposed, not yet approved.

nodes.label: Phase 0 Status (Not Started)
nodes.rationale: Audio engine, MIDI engine, project format, UI, plugin host, testing and release system are all NOT STARTED.

nodes.label: Absolute User Control Rule
nodes.rationale: Claude must not autonomously implement changes. 'continue', 'go ahead', 'do it', 'fix it' do not count as approval unless an exact plan was shown first.

nodes.label: Decision Log
nodes.rationale: Every major architectural decision recorded with context, options, tradeoffs and status; never silently replaced.

nodes.label: Definition of Done
nodes.rationale: A feature is not done because UI exists or code compiles; behavior, tests, edge cases, performance, docs and graph accuracy are all required.

nodes.label: Dependency Policy
nodes.rationale: No dependency without approval; name, purpose, license, maintenance, platform support, performance, security and alternatives must be presented first.

nodes.label: Required Feature Workflow (Steps A-E)
nodes.rationale: Graph, research, inspect current state, plan, then STOP and wait for explicit approval.

nodes.label: First Task: Discovery and Architecture Planning
nodes.rationale: On a fresh repository do not start coding; perform complete discovery and architecture planning, then stop.
nodes.norm_label: first task: discovery and architecture planning

nodes.label: Graphify Mandate
nodes.rationale: Graphify is a persistent architectural intelligence layer, not a one-time setup tool; it establishes structure before raw file reads so the repo is not blindly grepped.

nodes.label: Scope Control
nodes.rationale: If implementation reveals another problem, stop and report scope expansion instead of auto-fixing unrelated issues.

nodes.label: Critical Operating Rule
nodes.rationale: Default state is RESEARCH - GRAPHIFY - PLAN - STOP - USER APPROVAL - IMPLEMENT - VERIFY. Claude may investigate and plan autonomously but may not modify the codebase.

nodes.label: Development Rule (One Subsystem at a Time)
nodes.rationale: Never generate a fake complete DAW in one pass; no fake waveform editors, fake engines, placeholder mixer logic or dead UI buttons.
nodes.norm_label: development rule (one subsystem at a time)

nodes.label: First Session Discovery Objective
nodes.rationale: The next session must not start coding; it must perform environment and Graphify verification first.

nodes.label: Feature Implementation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Nine steps: Graphify, research, inspect, plan, STOP, implement, verify, Graphify update, handoff.

nodes.label: Graphify Workflow
nodes.rationale: Graph, inspect GRAPH_REPORT.md, query relationships, inspect only relevant files, plan. Never fake Graphify output.

nodes.label: Handoff Rule
nodes.rationale: Update HANDOFF.md after significant approved implementation; do not pretend the project is further along than it is.

nodes.label: PROTOTYPE / MOCK / PRODUCTION Labeling
nodes.rationale: Maturity must be stated explicitly so mocked behavior is never presented as complete functionality.

nodes.label: Content / Sound Library
nodes.rationale: Do not bundle copyrighted commercial content; use original, demo or public-domain assets.

nodes.label: Pattern System
nodes.rationale: Patterns must be reusable, independently editable, and placeable into the arrangement.

nodes.label: Piano Roll
nodes.rationale: First-class editing environment; performance must remain usable with very large note counts.

nodes.label: Proposed Architectural Layers
nodes.rationale: Twenty candidate layers from Platform to Persistence; the structure is NOT approved and must not be implemented blindly.

nodes.label: MPE Readiness
nodes.rationale: Architecture should be prepared for future MPE support rather than retrofitted later.

nodes.label: Performance Strategy
nodes.rationale: Performance is a feature; profile before optimizing and never optimize based on assumptions.

nodes.label: Performance Strategy
nodes.rationale: Performance work must be measured; no premature optimization.

nodes.label: Controller Linking
nodes.rationale: A single generic parameter mapping system rather than per-surface mappings.

nodes.label: Built-in Effect Framework
nodes.rationale: Effects must share a common DSP/plugin interface.

nodes.label: Plugin Host
nodes.rationale: Third-party plugins are never assumed safe; the host must be resilient to plugin crashes and invalid behavior.

nodes.label: Plugin Host Priority
nodes.rationale: The plugin system must be architected early even if complete support comes later.

nodes.label: Command Registry / Keyboard Shortcuts
nodes.rationale: Every action is a command; shortcuts must not be hardcoded inside UI components, keeping the system scripting-ready.

nodes.label: INCDAW
nodes.rationale: Must not be treated as a toy DAW, demo, prototype, mockup or UI-only app; architected so features can be added without rewriting the audio engine.

nodes.label: Built-in Instrument Framework
nodes.rationale: Build the instrument API first rather than attempting all instruments at once.

nodes.label: Platform Strategy
nodes.rationale: macOS and Windows targets; Linux must not be made impossible, and platform-specific code stays isolated.

nodes.label: Proposed Repository Structure
nodes.rationale: Do not use blindly; the final structure is determined by Graphify plus the actual repository state.

nodes.label: Time Stretching / Pitch Architecture
nodes.rationale: Must be pluggable with realtime preview and offline high-quality modes; a low-quality placeholder must not be considered complete.

nodes.label: Undo / Redo
nodes.rationale: Prefer a command-based architecture; avoid ad-hoc undo implementations.

nodes.label: Open Decisions
nodes.rationale: Language, UI framework, audio backend, DSP, plugin, cross-platform, serialization, rendering, threading, state, command, undo/redo, dependency and licensing architecture are all undecided; Claude recommends but must not decide silently.

nodes.label: Clip / Project Data Model
nodes.rationale: Distinct entity types must not be collapsed into one generic object.

nodes.label: Mixer
nodes.rationale: Routing must support arbitrary graph-like signal flow where safe; avoid hardcoded linear signal chains.

nodes.label: Offline Render Engine
nodes.rationale: Realtime and offline processing must use compatible DSP paths where possible.

nodes.label: Core Data Model
nodes.rationale: Project, Song, Timeline, Track, Clip, Pattern, Channel, Instrument, Plugin, Mixer Node, Automation, MIDI Event, Audio Asset, Routing Connection must stay distinct entities.

nodes.label: MIDI Signal Flow
nodes.rationale: MIDI to Instrument to Channel to Mixer to Effects to Automation to Master to Render.

nodes.label: INCDAW Project Format
nodes.rationale: Versioned, migratable, deterministic, portable, resilient to missing media; never create a project format without versioning.

nodes.label: Versioned Project Format
nodes.rationale: The project format must be versioned from day one (INCDAW_PROJECT_VERSION) so future migrations remain possible; never create an unversioned format.

nodes.label: Audio Engine
nodes.rationale: Critical subsystem; audio thread safety is a first-class architectural requirement.

nodes.label: UI Architecture
nodes.rationale: Modular dockable workspaces with INCDAW's own visual identity; do not copy FL Studio's exact visual design.

nodes.label: Audio Engine Priority
nodes.rationale: The audio engine is the foundation; realtime audio code must not depend on UI operations.

nodes.label: UI Priority
nodes.rationale: The UI must be decoupled from the audio engine.

nodes.label: Audio Correctness Requirements
nodes.rationale: Audio correctness is non-negotiable: sample-accurate timing, denormals, NaN/infinity, buffer and sample-rate changes, offline render equivalence.

nodes.label: Engineering Rules
nodes.rationale: No God classes, no circular dependencies, no UI/DSP coupling, no serialization inside UI, no routing logic in visual components.

nodes.label: Realtime Audio Thread Safety
nodes.rationale: The realtime audio thread must never allocate unnecessarily, block on I/O, do network operations, wait for UI, or take locks that risk priority inversion.

nodes.label: Testing Strategy
nodes.rationale: Every core subsystem needs automated tests; add a regression test for every serious bug.

nodes.label: Testing Strategy
nodes.rationale: Unit, integration, end-to-end and regression levels; every serious bug gets a regression test.

nodes.label: Automation Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Automation must be a generic subsystem; never build it separately for every plugin or control.

nodes.label: Playlist / Arrangement
nodes.rationale: Architecture must not assume a simplistic 1:1 track-to-mixer relationship; the routing model must stay flexible.

nodes.label: Audio Recording Signal Flow
nodes.rationale: Audio Input to Recording to Audio Clip to Playlist to Mixer to Effects to Automation to Master to Render.

nodes.label: Plugin Automation Flow
nodes.rationale: Plugin to Parameter to Automation to Mixer to Render.

nodes.label: Definition of Success
nodes.rationale: INCDAW should feel like a real professional DAW rather than a collection of disconnected tools.

nodes.label: Shared Transport / Timing / Undo Foundation
nodes.rationale: All systems must share the same underlying transport, timing, project state and undo architecture - this is what makes the three signal chains one DAW instead of three tools.

nodes.label: FL Studio 2026 Reference
nodes.rationale: Primary functional reference for analysis only; proprietary source, assets, plugins, presets and visual identity are out of bounds.
nodes.community_name: FL Studio Reference and IP Boundary

nodes.label: INCDAW Project Mission
nodes.rationale: Functional parity with FL Studio-class workflows using independent code, architecture, algorithms, assets, branding and UI.
nodes.community_name: FL Studio Reference and IP Boundary

nodes.label: FL Studio Feature Parity Objective
nodes.rationale: FL Studio is a functional reference for capabilities and workflows only; proprietary source, algorithms, assets, presets and branding must not be copied.
nodes.community_name: FL Studio Reference and IP Boundary

nodes.label: Legal / IP Boundary
nodes.rationale: Equivalent functionality is allowed; proprietary implementation, reverse-engineered internals, copyrighted assets and trademarks are not.
nodes.community_name: FL Studio Reference and IP Boundary
